value.lineage: Avida (1993-, Adami/Ofria/Brown, later Devosoft): a platform of self-replicating computer programs (digital organisms) that mutate, compete for CPU time, and evolve to perform logic tasks for rewards; the workhorse of experimental digital evolution

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: controlled experiments in the evolution of computation

value.built_to: let self-replicating programs (digital organisms) mutate and compete for CPU cycles and memory, rewarding those that evolve to compute logic functions -- an instrumented Petri dish for open-ended evolution
value.pressure: finite CPU and space; an organism must copy its own genome faster and more accurately than rivals while the reward landscape selects for new computation
value.success_means: in its domain, evolving populations that acquire new functions from mutation and selection; the published Avida experiments reproduce

inspected_files: cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc (instruction table, label search, single step, head-copy, head-search, if-label, divide main)
main/cBirthEntry.cc, main/cDeme.cc (the reference holders outside the arbiter)
cut.note: the famous name (Avida, digital evolution) covers a small closed loop: a virtual CPU whose programs copy themselves with per-instruction copy errors; a divide that is refused unless the copy is plausible; a merit that is genome size times a task bonus; a scheduler that hands out CPU cycles in proportion to merit; a placement rule that kills whoever occupies the chosen cell; and an environment that scores logic functions on the organism's own I/O. Everything else in 60k lines is a configuration-gated extension of one of those

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.mechanism: every instruction is a fixed-size opcode from a table; nop-A/B/C do nothing when executed but MODIFY the instruction before them (which register ?BX? means) and, in sequence, spell a LABEL that other instructions read by scanning the following nops (ReadLabel); so the same three symbols are the argument system and the addressing system, and every mutation lands on a legal instruction
organs.input: the genome as a sequence of opcodes
assumptions: a closed alphabet where every string is a valid program (no syntax errors) is what makes random mutation productive rather than fatal
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: mutational robustness by construction; labels give position-independent addressing so insertions and deletions do not break jumps
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a mutation inside a label changes what it matches, silently; the record's tasks are typically evolved with only 26 of the ~200 table entries enabled (the instruction set is a config file)
organs.human_prior: Ray's Tierra (1991) introduced nop-templates; Avida's three-nop alphabet and register modification are Ofria/Brown/Adami's redesign
organs.source_boundary: the s_n_array / s_f_array tables and ReadLabel

organs.mechanism: h-search reads the nop label that follows it, takes its COMPLEMENT (Rotate by 1 over the three nops: A->B, B->C, C->A) and searches the genome forward from the start for that complement, leaving the FLOW head after the match and the distance in BX; if-label compares the complement of the label just read with the label most recently copied, so a program can detect that it has finished copying its own end marker; a search that finds nothing leaves the head where it was
organs.input: a label read from the genome; the genome
organs.output: a head position; a skip decision
organs.state: the flow head; the read label
assumptions: complement matching means a program never matches its own search template accidentally; the default ancestor uses nop-A nop-B ... nop-C nop-A as the copy-loop markers
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the self-copy loop terminates by recognising its own end label rather than by counting; loops survive length changes
organs.human_prior: Tierra's template addressing; the complement rule is Avida's

organs.human_name: Inst_HeadCopy (7130-7175); the copy-time rates in cMutationRates
organs.mechanism: h-copy reads the instruction under the READ head, and with probability copy_mut_prob replaces it with a random instruction from the set before writing it under the WRITE head (flagging the site); then, each with its own probability, inserts a random instruction, deletes one, applies a uniform mutation, or SLIPS (jumps the read head or duplicates/deletes a stretch); both heads advance; the parent program itself decides when and where to copy
organs.input: the genome under the read head; the mutation rates
organs.output: one instruction written (possibly wrong) under the write head
organs.state: the read and write heads; per-site flags (copied, mutated)
assumptions: mutation is an error in the organism's OWN copying act, so an organism that copies less (or copies fewer sites) exposes itself to fewer errors -- the rate is per copied instruction, not per generation
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: variation is produced by the same machinery selection acts on; slip mutations give whole-block duplications (the source of length change)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an organism can evolve to skip copying part of itself (checked by the divide gate below)
organs.human_prior: copy-time error as THE mutation source (Tierra); Avida adds divide-time and inject-time classes
organs.source_boundary: Inst_HeadCopy and the copy-time TestCopy* probes

organs.mechanism: a divide instruction succeeds only if: the parent has executed at least JUV_PERIOD and MIN_CYCLES instructions; both halves are within OFFSPRING_SIZE_RANGE of the genome length and within absolute bounds; the parent executed at least MIN_EXE_LINES fraction of its length; the offspring has at least MIN_COPIED_LINES fraction of its sites actually written by h-copy; optionally the offspring must be an exact copy (REQUIRE_EXACT_COPY); then the memory is cropped at the divide point, divide-time mutations are applied, and the parent is reset
organs.input: the parent memory, the divide point, the execution/copy flags
organs.output: an offspring genome or a fault (divide fails, parent continues)
assumptions: a program that divides without copying (or after copying junk) is a cheat the world must refuse, or replication collapses to trivial short genomes
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: closes the shortcut of 'divide immediately'; the fractions are the world's minimum notion of a real copy
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: the thresholds are constants, so an organism can sit exactly at MIN_COPIED_LINES
organs.human_prior: the size-range and copied-fraction gates are Avida-specific anti-cheat rules (not in Tierra)

organs.mechanism: after a successful divide the offspring genome receives, independently: slip, transposition, lateral-gene-transfer, point, insertion, deletion, uniform mutations, each drawn either per site (binomial over genome length, divided by a mut_multiplier), or at most once per divide, or Poisson with a constant genomic mean; parent mutations (applied to the parent's own memory) exist too; meta-mutation can perturb the copy-mutation rate itself
organs.input: the offspring genome; the rate table
assumptions: divide-time mutation decouples variation from the copy act (a different evolutionary regime from copy-time error, selectable by config)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: experiments can hold the genomic mutation rate constant across genome lengths (the Poisson class) -- a control the copy-time class cannot offer
organs.human_prior: the per-site vs per-genome distinction is the experimenter's, encoded as three rate families

organs.mechanism: merit = base x bonus, where base is a size measure chosen by BASE_MERIT_METHOD (copied size, executed size, full length, least of them, sqrt of least, or a bonus-instruction count) and bonus starts at DEFAULT_BONUS and is modified by reactions during the organism's life; the product is locked in when the organism divides (DivideReset) and the offspring is born with the parent's merit (INHERIT_MERIT) or the bare size merit; fitness (for statistics, not for selection) is merit_base x bonus / gestation_time
organs.input: size counts; the bonus from the environment; gestation time
organs.output: merit (the scheduler's priority); fitness (a reported number)
organs.update: bonus per reaction; merit per divide
assumptions: size in the base term compensates for the fact that a longer genome needs more cycles to copy: without it, the shortest replicator always wins
merit is inherited so a lineage's rewards persist until its offspring earn their own
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one scalar carries both 'how much work is a copy' and 'what has this program computed'; selection acts on the product
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with BASE_MERIT_FULL_SIZE an organism gains merit by growing junk; the LEAST_SIZE options exist because of that
organs.human_prior: merit x bonus, and merit/gestation as fitness, are Avida's central design decisions (Ofria & Wilke 2004)
organs.source_boundary: the merit fields of cPhenotype and their two writers

organs.human_name: cEnvironment::DoProcesses (1610-1760); the reaction process types (170-176); cTaskLib::AddTask (73-142)
organs.mechanism: when an organism's output matches a task on its inputs (the library: echo, add, sub, not, nand, and, orn, or, andn, nor, xor, equ, three-input logic 3AA-3AV, ...), each reaction process computes consumed = min(max, resource available x max_fraction) x task_quality, and bonus = consumed x value; the bonus is applied to the phenotype as ADD, MULT (bonus *= value), POW (bonus *= 2^value), LIN (value x task count), or into energy; resources may be depletable (a finite pool shared by the population) or unlimited (resource NULL: consumed = max x quality)
organs.input: the organism's I/O history; the environment's reaction list; resource levels
assumptions: logic functions on 32-bit inputs are the world's notion of computation; the 'nand' primitive is the only logic instruction, so every other function must be built from it
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the reward structure (multiplicative doubling by task complexity in the classic EQU experiments) is what makes complex functions evolve from simpler ones (Lenski et al. 2003)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with unlimited resources the bonus is a pure function of the genome; with depletable resources it is frequency-dependent
organs.human_prior: the logic-9 environment and its 2^n reward ladder are the experimenter's world design, not the organism's

organs.mechanism: every cell's priority is its organism's merit (times a deme merit if any); the INTEGRATED scheduler decomposes each merit into powers of two and alternates 'the best' with 'everything else' recursively so that time slices are spread as evenly as possible while honouring the ratios; the PROBABILISTIC scheduler draws the next cell with probability proportional to merit; ROUND_ROBIN ignores merit; each schedule step executes ONE instruction of the chosen organism
organs.input: merits; a clock of instruction slots
organs.update: per instruction executed and per merit change
assumptions: CPU cycles are the only currency; an organism's reproductive rate is its merit divided by the cycles a copy costs
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: selection is implemented as scheduling: nothing 'chooses' survivors, higher merit simply runs more often
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the integrated scheduler is deterministic given merits, so identical-merit populations execute in a fixed order (a hidden bias the probabilistic scheduler removes at the cost of variance)
organs.human_prior: merit-proportional time slicing (Adami/Brown 1994) is the ecological law of the world; the binary-decomposition trick is an implementation choice
organs.source_boundary: the scheduler classes and the three cPopulation methods

organs.mechanism: a newborn is assigned a cell by BIRTH_METHOD: a random cell in the whole population (optionally preferring empty cells), the ELDEST cell via a reaper queue, a random cell in the parent's deme, the cell the parent faces, a neighbourhood cell (handlers), or a migration target; population caps kill a random or the oldest organism first; then ActivateOrganism KILLS whatever occupies the target cell and inserts the newborn; death is therefore mostly replacement, not aging
assumptions: space is the second finite resource; a full world means every birth is a death
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the geometry of placement (well-mixed vs neighbourhood) is what makes spatial structure an experimental variable
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: FULL_SOUP_RANDOM with a full world gives every organism the same expected lifetime regardless of merit, so selection acts only through birth rate
organs.human_prior: the birth-method menu is the experimenter's; 'kill the occupant' is Tierra's reaper generalised
organs.source_boundary: PositionOffspring and the KillOrganism call in ActivateOrganism

organs.mechanism: if DEATH_METHOD is on, each organism draws at birth a maximum instruction count = AGE_LIMIT + N(0,1) x AGE_DEVIATION, optionally multiplied by genome length; an organism that executes more than that dies regardless of merit
assumptions: a lifetime cap prevents an immortal non-replicating high-merit organism from holding a cell forever
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the only death that is not replacement; off by default
organs.source_boundary: the DEATH_METHOD block in cOrganism's constructor

organs.human_name: Genotype::ClassifyNewUnit (Genotype.cc 282-299); GenotypeArbiter::ClassifyNewUnit (GenotypeArbiter.cc 278-369); the founder constructor (Genotype.cc 128-184); Matches (406-456)
organs.mechanism: a newborn is offered to its parent's genotype. Same genome: it joins that genotype and NOTHING is recorded but a count (breed true). Different genome: the arbiter searches the hash of LIVING genotypes for an identical genome (same hardware type, instruction set and transmission class); if one exists the newborn joins it and who bore it is not recorded. Only if none exists is a new genotype founded: id = a counter that only increments, parents = the parental genotype(s), depth = first parent's depth + 1, update_born = the arbiter's clock. That founding is the ONLY moment a parent edge is written. Because only living genotypes are searched, a genome that re-arises while its genotype lives is absorbed into it, while the same genome re-arising after that genotype died founds a second genotype with a new id
organs.input: a newborn unit's genome and source; its parent's genotype(s)
organs.output: the unit's genotype; at most one new record with one parent edge
organs.state: a hash of living genotypes by genome; the next id; per-genotype counts
organs.update: per birth and per inject (an injected unit is classified with no parents and founds a ROOT)
assumptions: identity is exact genome equality, so descent is recorded between CLASSES of identical organisms, never between organisms
a class is founded once; later arrivals by mutation from elsewhere are the same class
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: memory and bookkeeping scale with distinct genomes, not with births; the dominant genotype is one record however many organisms carry it
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the recorded tree is a tree of FIRST APPEARANCES. Convergent and back-mutation births leave no edge, so gene flow into an existing class is invisible; sequence is not a key across time (a revived genome gets a new id); with DISABLE_GENOTYPE_CLASSIFICATION every genotype is founded parentless (GenotypeArbiter.cc 348-352)
organs.human_prior: genotype-as-class bookkeeping as written by David M. Bryson, 2009-2011 (the file headers); whether other platforms keep an organism-level pedigree instead was not checked
organs.source_boundary: the two ClassifyNewUnit methods, the founder constructor and Matches

organs.human_name: GenotypeArbiter::removeGenotype (GenotypeArbiter.cc 498-533), AdjustGenotype (372-410), PerformUpdate (85-103); Genotype::RemoveUnit (Genotype.cc 321-331); Group reference counts (Group.cc 46-49)
organs.mechanism: every genotype carries an ACTIVE count (its living units) and a PASSIVE count (the child genotypes that name it as parent). When the last unit dies the genotype is deactivated, stamped with update_deactivated and moved to a 'historic' list. If nothing passive refers to it, each of its parents loses one passive reference and is examined in turn, recursively, and the genotype is unlinked for good. So at every instant memory holds exactly the living genotypes and the ancestors of the living; a lineage with no living descendant disappears when its last leaf does, not at the end of the run
organs.output: the set of retained genotype records
organs.state: two counters per genotype; the historic list
organs.update: per death, recursively up the parent chain; a sweep at the end of every update
assumptions: what will be asked of the record is the line of descent of what survives; extinct side branches are not worth their memory
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a run of any length keeps memory proportional to the living population's ancestry, not to every genotype ever founded
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an event that replaces organisms with INJECTED copies severs the record entirely -- the injects are roots, the old tree loses its last units and is pruned to nothing, though every new organism is a physical descendant of an old one (PopulationActions.cc 153-171). Two holders outside the arbiter break the invariant in opposite directions: a deme's founder/germline hold is PASSIVE (cDeme.cc 958, 985), so a dead leaf survives; a waiting sexual birth entry's hold is ACTIVE (cBirthChamber.cc 159-161), so a genotype with no organism stays 'living', is on neither list, and is written by nobody
organs.human_prior: UNKNOWN beyond this body; here the pruning is unconditional (no configuration switch keeps the full tree: DISABLE_GENOTYPE_CLASSIFICATION only removes more)

organs.human_name: cPopulation::SavePopulation (cPopulation.cc 6362-6563); Genotype::LegacySave (Genotype.cc 356-392); GenotypeArbiter::LegacySave (123-131); Output::File (File.cc 183-252); the SavePopulation action (SaveLoadActions.cc 138-183)
organs.mechanism: walks the cells, groups living organisms by genotype, and writes one line per living genotype: id, source, source arguments, parent id(s), living units, total units ever, length, mean merit / gestation / fitness, generation and update born, update deactivated, depth, hardware type, instruction set, sequence -- then the cells it occupies and per-organism offsets. Then, unless save_historic=0 (the default is 1), one line for every genotype on the historic list: the same first seventeen columns and nothing else. The header's #format line is taken from the first row written
organs.input: the cell array; the arbiter's historic list
organs.output: a text file, one genotype per line
assumptions: a population is restorable from genotypes plus cell lists; organisms of one genotype are interchangeable except for position and gestation offset
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the save is at once a checkpoint and the run's phylogeny (the line of descent of every survivor, with sequences)
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: fields are separated by single spaces and src_args is written raw, so a source argument containing spaces ('whole-genome duplication', PopulationActions.cc 169) shifts every later column of that row; a living genotype with no organism in a cell (held only by a birth entry) is written nowhere; with save_historic=0 parent ids point at rows that are not in the file; rows are NOT in ancestral order (living rows in hash-map order, 6466, then the historic list), so a parent's row may follow its child's; the #format line names the twenty columns of a living row while historic rows carry seventeen
organs.human_prior: the .spop (Structured POPulation) format; its columns are the experimenter's notion of what a genotype is
organs.source_boundary: SavePopulation and the three LegacySave methods

organs.human_name: cPopulation::LoadPopulation (cPopulation.cc 6820-7032); the load constructor (Genotype.cc 187-263); GenotypeArbiter::LegacyLoad (133-138) and the id-hint path of ClassifyNewUnit (290-332)
organs.mechanism: reads every row, sorts them by id, and re-creates the genotypes oldest first with FRESH ids from the arbiter's counter; each row's parent list is rewritten to the new ids of parents already re-created, and a parent id that names no row in the file is dropped without a message (the warning is commented out, 6996). Then num_units organisms are injected per row with an id hint, which makes the arbiter reactivate that genotype instead of founding one
organs.output: a population and an arbiter state
assumptions: a file saved with historic rows reloads its whole line of descent; one saved without them reloads as unrelated roots, and that is acceptable
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: runs can be resumed and populations transplanted between experiments
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a save_historic=0 file loads with every living genotype whose parent is extinct turned into a ROOT that keeps its old depth (depth is read from the file, the parent is gone); ids are not stable across a save/load; the loaded organisms' source argument becomes the file name (6858-6861)
organs.human_prior: checkpoint/restart; the silent degradation of ancestry on load is an implementation choice, not a documented one
organs.source_boundary: LoadPopulation's parent-fix loop (6968-6995, after the sort at 6960-6962) and the hinted classification

organs.human_name: m_cur_update (GenotypeArbiter.cc 49, 87); the driver loop (Avida2Driver.cc 91-162); event triggers (cEventList.cc 127-202)
organs.mechanism: the arbiter's clock starts at -1 and is set to (update just completed + 1) at the END of each update; the driver fires the events for update T after update T has been processed and before the counter advances. So a genotype founded before the run or during update 0 is stamped -1; one founded while update u >= 1 runs is stamped u; one founded by an event scheduled at update T is stamped T+1; and no genotype is ever stamped 0
assumptions: the stamp is for statistics (age = current update - update born), where an off-by-one at the origin is harmless
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a time base for genotype age
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a reconstruction that orders genotypes by update_born cannot separate 'before the run' from 'during update 0', and sees an event-injected genotype as one update younger than a genotype founded in the update the event fired after; update_deactivated = -1 means 'alive' and also 'died during update 0'

organs.mechanism: after each pruning step, walk from the most abundant genotype up its FIRST parents to the root; the last genotype met that is alive or is named by more than one retained child is the coalescent, and its depth is published. Below it the retained tree is a single file of dead genotypes with one child each, so it is the most recent common ancestor of everything retained -- provided everything retained descends through that line
organs.update: per pruned genotype, skipped while the current coalescent still qualifies (537)
assumptions: asexual: only first parents are followed (the source says so, 545)
one ancestor: with several injected roots the walk follows only the dominant's line
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the depth of the population's common ancestor, read without a tree traversal at analysis time
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with two retained roots the 'coalescent' is the common ancestor of one root's descendants only
organs.human_prior: coalescence depth as a run statistic (Avida's 'coalescent depth')

organs.human_name: cBirthChamber::SubmitOffspring sexual branch (cBirthChamber.cc 443-587); DoBasicRecombination (286-313); RegionSwap / GenomeSwap (178-224); DoPairAsexBirth (264-282); SetupGenotypeInfo (435-441)
organs.mechanism: an offspring from a sexual divide waits in the birth chamber until a second one arrives. Then two random fractions of genome length are drawn, the region between them is cut out of BOTH genomes at the same fractions (so unequal lengths are allowed and the pieces may differ in size) and exchanged; merit is blended by the exchanged fraction; if more than half was exchanged the two results swap labels, so each child is named after the parent it took the MAJORITY from. Two children are built (or one, chosen by coin, under a two-fold cost), and each is classified with BOTH parents' genotypes, its majority parent first -- which is therefore the parent its depth is counted from. With MODULE_NUM > 0 the cut points are module boundaries, contiguous, independent per module, or shuffled between modules
organs.input: two offspring genomes and their parents' genotypes and merits; two uniform draws
organs.output: two (or one) recombinant genomes, each with an ordered pair of parent genotypes
organs.update: per sexual divide that finds a waiting entry
assumptions: homology is positional and proportional: the same FRACTION of two genomes is treated as the same place
one exchanged region is enough; the operator is symmetric in the two parents
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: recombination between programs of different lengths without alignment; the modular variants test whether exchange at module boundaries preserves function
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the OPERATOR LEAVES NO RECORD -- the two fractions, the module choices and whether the labels were swapped are drawn, used and discarded; the save keeps only the two parent ids. A swap refused for illegal length (RegionSwap 192-196) still blends merit and still records two parents for a child that is genetically one parent's. A child identical to its first parent's genotype, or to any living genotype, is absorbed and records no parents at all. When recombination is skipped (RECOMBINATION_PROB, or zero cross points) the pair is born as two single-parent children (DoPairAsexBirth). Under ENERGY_ENABLED with a two-fold cost, line 576 reads child_array[1] of a one-element array
organs.human_prior: two-point crossover (the GA operator), located by fraction rather than by index so that variable-length programs can be crossed; the modular variants are Avida's (Misevic, Ofria, Lenski on sex and modularity, recalled not checked)
organs.source_boundary: DoBasicRecombination + RegionSwap + the two SetupGenotypeInfo calls at 553-554

pressures.source_evidence: record human_capability_summary; cHardwareCPU Inst_HeadCopy; cHardwareBase Divide_CheckViable; cPhenotype DivideReset; Apto Integrated scheduler; cPopulation PositionOffspring
pressures.condition: the world executes many programs a few instructions at a time; a program persists only by producing a copy of itself that passes a plausibility gate; each copied symbol is corrupted with a fixed probability; the share of execution a lineage receives is proportional to a score that starts at its length and multiplies when its inputs and outputs satisfy functions the world names
pressures.resource_or_constraint: instruction slots per world step; cells (a copy needs an empty or killed cell); a mutation rate per copied symbol
pressures.failure_condition: no lineage replicates within the run (the ancestor is lost), or the population collapses to minimal replicators that compute nothing
pressures.world_punishes: long genomes (more to copy per cycle) and computation that does not pay in score; slow copiers under replacement death
pressures.world_rewards: lineages whose copy is fast and accurate enough AND whose extra instructions earn multiplicative score
pressures.observable_consequence: fraction of runs in which any named function appears by generation G; genome length and per-site mutation load over time; time to the highest-value function as the reward ladder's base (ADD vs MULT vs POW) is varied
pressures.vacuity_condition: no copy error (nothing varies), or unlimited CPU and space (no competition), or a score independent of computation
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a program that divides without copying (closed by the copied-fraction gate); a world that rewards length alone
pressures.cheat_control: an organism handed the full score directly (bonus injected) must dominate the population within a few generations without computing anything -- if it does not, the scheduler is not reading merit; a non-replicating organism must vanish within one replacement cycle -- if it persists, death is not replacement
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: experimental digital evolution (Adami, Ofria, Brown; Avida 1993-)

pressures.condition: the world names a set of functions with values; an organism's score is the composition (add, multiply, or 2^value) of the rewards of every function it performs; complex functions are built from simpler ones the same programs already perform
pressures.resource_or_constraint: the score is the only lever on CPU share; the functions cost instructions to perform
pressures.failure_condition: the most complex function never appears because its stepping stones are not rewarded, or because rewards for stepping stones saturate
pressures.world_punishes: a ladder whose intermediate rungs pay nothing
pressures.observable_consequence: appearance rate of the top function across reward compositions (Lenski et al. 2003 shape: EQU evolves only when simpler functions are rewarded)
pressures.vacuity_condition: one function, or additive rewards so small that score is dominated by length
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: rewarding the top function directly at a value that dwarfs length
pressures.cheat_control: a world rewarding only the top function must show it evolving rarely or never; the same world with the compounding ladder must show it often: if the difference is not visible, the ladder is not the operative pressure
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: evolution of complex features (Lenski, Ofria, Pennock, Adami 2003)

pressures.condition: N cells; a newborn takes a cell and its occupant dies; the cell is chosen at random (well-mixed), by age (eldest), or by neighbourhood (spatial); no organism dies for being unfit -- it dies because a neighbour reproduced
pressures.failure_condition: a lineage that reproduces slowly is replaced before it reproduces even when its score is high (score buys cycles, not immunity)
pressures.world_rewards: short gestation relative to neighbours; in spatial worlds, local clustering
pressures.observable_consequence: lineage persistence vs gestation time under each placement rule; spatial correlation of genotypes under neighbourhood placement vs well-mixed
pressures.vacuity_condition: more cells than organisms (nobody is replaced)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given a cell that is excluded from placement must never die and must not spread: the world must show both, or placement is not the death mechanism
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: population structure in digital evolution (Avida birth methods)

pressures.source_evidence: GenotypeArbiter removeGenotype 498-533; Genotype founder constructor 153-177; cPopulation SavePopulation 6557-6560
pressures.condition: a population turns over thousands of times; nearly every lineage founded goes extinct; whoever reads the run afterwards wants to know how the survivors came to be; memory and the save file are finite
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one record per retained class of identical organisms; a run founds far more classes than it ever holds alive
pressures.failure_condition: memory grows with every class ever founded and the run dies, or a survivor's line of descent cannot be read back
pressures.world_punishes: keeping every record (unbounded growth); keeping none (no history)
pressures.world_rewards: keeping exactly the living classes and their ancestors, and forgetting an extinct branch as soon as its last member dies
pressures.observable_consequence: in a saved population, dead records that no record names as a parent: none under this rule, the large majority of dead records without it; retained records / records ever founded falls as the run lengthens
pressures.vacuity_condition: no extinction (nothing to forget) or no mutation (one class, no tree)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: found every class parentless (DISABLE_GENOTYPE_CLASSIFICATION); write only the living (save_historic=0)
pressures.cheat_control: the same population run with forgetting switched off must show dead unnamed records in its save; if it shows none, the observable cannot see forgetting and a zero in the real save means nothing (run on the reference model, nyx/atlas/experiments/avida_ancestry: 92 unnamed dead records of 131 with forgetting off, 0 of 23 with it on)
pressures.cost_class: memory-scale; the check on a saved file is milliseconds
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: phylogeny and line-of-descent analysis of digital evolution runs
